lesson_title: Income Tax, UIF and Exchange Rates: the Ladder and the Price Tag
hook_text: "Don't take the raise — the tax bracket will eat it." Your uncle is wrong, and one ladder proves it.
clip_script: Everyone knows someone who refused a raise because of the tax bracket. Here's the truth: income tax is a LADDER. Your first R237 100 for the year is taxed at 18 cents in the rand — always. Climb into the next bracket and only the money ABOVE that line pays 26 cents. The rands on the lower rungs are never re-taxed. Zanele earns R342 000. The table already worked out the first rung: R42 678. Her slice above the line is R104 900, taxed at 26 percent — R27 274. Add the rungs: R69 952. Then the part nobody tells you: the government hands every taxpayer a discount, the rebate, R17 235 off. She truly owes R52 717 — about R4 393 a month, taken as PAYE before payday. Multiply her WHOLE salary by 26 percent and you'd claim R88 920 — nineteen thousand rand of tax that doesn't exist. Brackets tax slices, not salaries. So when the raise comes? Take it. Every new rand keeps at least 74 cents. The ladder never eats a raise — only the slice on top pays more.
visual_style: A ladder rising through chalk-drawn tax bands, rand coins stacking on each rung and keeping their colour as the salary climbs; a red stamp crossing out R88 920; a payslip assembling line by line to end at net pay.
mood: Myth-busting and reassuring, the voice of someone who reads the tax table so the family does not have to.
pacing: Quick through the myth, steady rung by rung up the ladder, a firm slow beat on the R88 920 error and the final take-the-raise verdict.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read your own payslip like a pro.
